characters.name: Dave Gold
characters.description: An insurance salesman, married to Vicky. Abusive Parents: Other than being overly controlling, Dave often belittles and insults his kids (and their friends) to their faces. Amazingly Embarrassing Parent: Always. When his daughter Hillary lacks the courage to break up with her boyfriend, she introduces him to her perpetually embarrassing father Dave, hoping to turn off the boy. Boyfriend-Blocking Dad: He constantly gets in the way of Hillary's dating life, often intimidating the boys who are interested in her. Deadpan Snarker: While all the Gold family members tend to snark back, Dave does it more than everyone else. He snarks at his family almost all the time.

characters.name: Vicky Gold
characters.description: A part-time receptionist, married to Dave. The Conscience: Vicky tries to keep Dave's jerkishness and questionable parenting under some measure of control. She frequently argues with him as a result. Not So Above It All: While usually more reasonable than her husband (especially with their kids), even Vicky can be irritable and insensitive at times. Only Sane Woman: In the family. Since Dave, Hillary, and Mike tend to be selfish jerks, and Larry is rather eccentric, Vicky is easily the most normal person in the house. Parents as People: Her parenting skills are far from perfect and she can make mistakes, but Vicky is still a more reasonable parent than Dave, because she is more open-minded. Which is not that hard.

characters.name: Hillary Gold
characters.description: A teenage girl and the oldest of the Gold children. Big Sister Bully: Especially to Larry. She thinks he is a loser and wants him to stay away from her at school (though the younger brother Mike treats him just as badly). Book Dumb: Hillary struggles academically because she cares more about her social life rather than studying, but she is not particularly stupid. Bratty Teenage Daughter: A classic example, being a selfish 16-year-old drama queen who frequently yells "I hate you!" to her parents, and sneaks out of the house to go to parties. Dating What Daddy Hates: Her boyfriends of the week frequently cause conflict with her overprotective father Dave.

characters.name: Larry Gold
characters.description: The odd middle child. All of the Other Reindeer: Larry is an outcast at school, outside of hisOnly FriendKenny. Even his siblings put him down and avoid him. Camp Straight: He alarms his father with his non-macho behavior, such as participating in the school musical and dressing as a woman. Dave suspects that he and his nerdy best friend, Kenny, are more than friends. It turns out that Larry is straight... but Kenny isn't. Jerkass Ball: Larry is usually meek compared to his siblings, but he still has his bratty moments towards his parents or during hisSibling Rivalryfights. Jock Dad, Nerd Son: He is a dorky boy with geeky interests (like science fiction, fantasy, and musicals), while his father Dave would prefer Larry to act more like a "manly man".

characters.name: Mike Gold
characters.description: The youngest of the Gold children. Annoying Younger Sibling: To Larry and Hillary. As Mike admits in hisInner Monologueof an episode, he enjoys trolling them and mocking them. Deadpan Snarker: Like his father Dave, Mike constantly snarks at the rest of the family. Dirty Kid: As revealed in one episode, Mike has already started masturbating when he is still in middle school. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Despite his rebellious attitude and bad behavior, even Mike has his nice moments. For example, giving Hillary advice about one of her boyfriends.

characters.name: Kenny Al-Bahir
characters.description: Drop-In Character: Being Larry's friend, he is frequently seen at the Golds' house. He even lives with the Golds for a while, after his parents have kicked him out for being gay. Give Geeks a Chance: He is just as geeky as Larry. By the end of the series, he starts dating Dylan. Incompatible Orientation: Initially, Kenny has a crush on his friend Larry, but the latter is straight. Only Friend: Being awkward nerds, he and Larry are this to each other. Promotion to Opening Titles: One of the fastest on record: Rami Malek was added to the opening credits starting in the show's second episode, though only for the episodes in which his character appeared. (This ended up being about half of them.)
